name: Poison
summary: A permanent-for-the-fight stacking debuff that deals 1 damage per stack every 2 seconds.
playNote: Poison is a long-fight engine. Early application and effects that read total Poison matter more than a late one-time stack.

name: Burn
summary: A stacking debuff that deals 1 damage per stack every second and loses one stack after each tick.
playNote: Burn rewards repeated application. One large stack falls away, while frequent smaller applications keep the pressure active.

name: Frost
summary: Each stack reduces Attack Speed and Defense by 0.5, then one stack dissipates every 2 seconds.
playNote: Frost is both mitigation and damage support. Apply it before the enemy's main attack cycle and before your carry's burst.

name: Stun
summary: The affected enemy cannot act for a fixed duration. The default is 1.5 seconds, while named abilities may last longer.
playNote: Stun is most valuable when it interrupts an opening threat or buys enough time for a first cast, not merely when it adds raw duration.

name: Anti-Heal
summary: Reduces all healing received by the affected unit to half value.
playNote: Anti-Heal matters against sustain loops. It does not deal damage by itself, so pair it with enough pressure to exploit the reduced recovery.

name: Stealth
summary: A Stealthed hero cannot be selected by normal enemy targeting, although already launched projectiles and certain random abilities can still hit.
playNote: Stealth changes who receives pressure. Check which ally becomes the next valid target before treating it as pure defense.

name: Taunt
summary: Forces enemies to store the Taunting hero as their target until another effect replaces it or targeting is recalculated.
playNote: Taunt protects the formation only when the Taunter can absorb the redirected pressure. It will not pull back an attack whose windup already began.

name: Shields
summary: Temporary hit points that absorb normal, true, and damage-over-time damage before HP.
playNote: Shield timing is crucial. A large shield that expires before enemy burst may be weaker than a smaller shield applied at the right moment.

name: Rush
summary: A Rush (N) effect is active during the first N seconds of combat, then turns off unless a hero-specific effect refreshes it.
playNote: Rush builds must convert the opening window into a kill, control advantage, or permanent scaling before the timer closes.

name: Stall
summary: A Stall (N) effect turns on once at N seconds into combat and remains active for the rest of that fight.
playNote: Stall is a durability check. Do not choose a powerful Stall payoff if the current board cannot reliably reach its trigger time.

name: Omnivamp
summary: Heals the damage dealer for a percentage of all post-Defense damage dealt by attacks and abilities.
playNote: Omnivamp needs real damage uptime. It is not reliable protection for a hero that is controlled, out of range, or killed before acting.

name: Backup
summary: A Backup effect remains active while its hero is in reserve rather than fielded on the combat board.
playNote: Backup effects make the sixth roster slot valuable. Compare that passive contribution against fielding the hero directly.
